thread:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 streaming latency breach for model 'redwood-embed-large' on cluster gpu-pool-4. Current p99=12.4s, p95=3.1s. Streaming stalls observed (connections stuck in 'sending' state). Auto-escalation to #incidents. Paging oncall.

anika: I'm oncall, grabbing context. Which nodes/shards are hot?

ops-bot: Top affected shard: gpu-pool-4/az-west-2b. Hot tenant id(s): tenant-8823 (large batch) and tenant-119 (bursting). IO saturation visible on NVMe host devices. Short dump: 
```
iostat -x 1 3
Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rsec/s  wsec/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         0.00   0.10 120.00  50.00  9600.00  800.00   84.62    6.22  48.40  12.10  65.00   2.60  98.50
```

anika: yikes. Looks like host NVMe at 98% util. Are we seeing cgroup clamp events / blkio throttling?

jules: Confirming cgroup writeback spikes and blkio backlog on the host. I pulled dmesg and see repeated write timeouts tied to tenant containers.

anika: Priority is to stop customer-visible degradation. Options: 1) Evict tenant-8823 from pool (force migrate), 2) Apply IO throttle via cgroup for tenant-8823, 3) Route streaming traffic off the pool to fallback region/model. Thoughts?

tom: Eviction first if quick. We can patch scheduler to drain that tenant's jobs to dv-pool-2/az-west-2a. If migration will take >30s for some long-running streams, we should throttle.

jules: I can apply a temporary blkio throttle to tenant-8823. Command I'm going to run (will run only after ack):
```
sudo cgset -r blkio.throttle.read_bps_device="8:0 10485760" tenant-8823
sudo cgset -r blkio.throttle.write_bps_device="8:0 5242880" tenant-8823
```

anika: go for it, do the throttle + start drain. Notify customer-sre to pre-warn customers if migration may drop streams.

customer-sre: Heads up, tenant-8823 maps to customer 'Orchid Labs' (paid enterprise), tenant-119 is internal test. Orchid is likely experiencing degraded realtime responses. I'm opening a quick support note and will DM their SRE.

priyanka: PM note: Which customers are impacted and do we have SLA exposure? We need to know if we should escalate to account execs.

customer-sre: Orchid (tenant-8823) has ~30 active websocket sessions, some realtime transcription jobs. SLA is 99.9% for p99 latency; this is currently violating. Will alert account execs if not mitigated in 15m.

ops-bot: Running automated mitigation: setting route fallback for new streaming sessions away from gpu-pool-4 to gpu-pool-1. Existing sessions will remain until handoff/evac.

jules: Throttle applied to tenant-8823. I also bumped kernel dirty ratio on host to avoid massive writeback pauses: 
```
echo 40 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_ratio
```

anika: Starting drain of tenant-8823 jobs now. Tom, can you confirm scheduler patch?

tom: Patch applied to scheduler: set placement override for tenant-8823 to dv-pool-2 for 10m. Triggering graceful migration. CLI: 
```
redwoodctl migrate --tenant tenant-8823 --to dv-pool-2 --graceful --timeout 180
```

anika: Monitoring p99 now...

(2m pass)

jules: Host NVMe util dropped to 65%. p99 streaming latency trending down. Current p99=2.1s, p95=0.9s. Streaming stalls count reduced by 85%.

anika: Good. Customer-sre, can you confirm Orchid's observed impact?

customer-sre: Orchid reported intermittent slowdowns but reconnects successful. They've temporarily rerouted some critical trafﬁc as a precaution. No major data loss. I'll keep them updated.

priyanka: For post-incident follow-up: need root cause hypothesis, impact window, and owner for mitigation work. Also flag to billing for possible SLA credit.

jules: Immediate root cause: noisy tenant IO causing host-level NVMe saturation -> writeback/backpressure -> streaming stalls. Short-term fix: throttle/evict + scheduler routing. Long-term: add tenant-level IO isolation at admission and auto-evac on sustained latency.

anika: Agreed. Action items captured: 
- jules: run diagnostics and collect host iostat/dmesg + timeline (owner)
- tom: add auto-evac policy + safer default scheduler placement for heavy-IO tenants (owner)
- priyanka: coordinate customer comms and SLA/billing review (owner)
- customer-sre: log customer timeline & impact (owner)

ops-bot: Incident severity upgraded to Sev2. Creating incident page: https://incidents.redwood.internal/6187654321 (placeholder)

anika: Closing active paging — mitigation in place, p99 back under SLO for now. We'll keep monitoring for 30m. If things regress, re-open. Thanks all. :handshake:

(30m later)

jules: Verified stable: p99=0.8s, no streaming stalls. We'll keep throttle in place for 10m then remove gradually while monitoring. Full postmortem will be scheduled for tomorrow.

anika: Thanks. I'll mark this as resolved in oncall notes and hand to postmortem channel.

customer-sre: Orchid notified with timeline + mitigation notes. They'll accept follow-up postmortem.

priyanka: Adding follow-up: implement auto-detection of host NVMe util >85% -> trigger tenant slow-path and alert before SLO crosses.

jules: I'll attach logs and a host-level timeline to the incident page.

anika: resolving thread. :white_check_mark:
